facts.raw_span: A 19-year-old man with hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use
altered mental status
febrile and intermittently responsive (Glasgow Coma Scale 10)
left upper- and lower-limb weakness (strength 2/5 and 3/5)
leukocytosis (white blood cell count rising from 10.0 to 14.6 × 10^3/µL)
Urine toxicology was positive for benzodiazepines and opiates
Noncontrast head CT demonstrated a hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect but no hemorrhage

Brain MRI revealed T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule with mild surrounding edema, scattered small foci of restricted diffusion, and subtle punctate blooming on susceptibility-weighted images
Lumbar puncture yielded an opening pressure of 23 cm H₂O and slightly hazy cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) with 538 WBCs/mm³
no valvular vegetations
Gram stain was negative
Repeat MRI demonstrated progression with new involvement of the left basal ganglia, increased diffusion restriction, development of necrosis, and new peripheral contrast enhancement

concepts.preferred_label: Subacute bacterial endocarditis with embolic stroke
concepts.why: The patient has hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use, which increases the risk of endocarditis, and the presence of leukocytosis, fever, and embolic phenomena on imaging suggests an infectious etiology.
The patient has a hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect and surrounding edema, and the presence of leukocytosis and fever suggests a pyogenic infection.
The patient has altered mental status, fever, and leukocytosis, and the presence of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule suggests an inflammatory process.
The patient has left upper- and lower-limb weakness and the presence of a hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect suggests an ischemic event.
The patient has a history of intravenous heroin use and the presence of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule suggests a toxic etiology.
The patient has hepatitis C and altered mental status, and the presence of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule suggests a metabolic disorder.

aliases: vasculitis of the central nervous system
concepts.why: The patient has left upper- and lower-limb weakness and the presence of a hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect suggests an inflammatory process affecting the blood vessels.
The patient has hepatitis C and altered mental status, and the presence of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule suggests a demyelinating disease.

rationales.F01: Hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use may contribute to various neurological conditions, but the presence of these factors alone does not strongly rule in or out any of the listed concepts.
rationales.F06: Toxic leukoencephalopathy is a strong consideration given the patient's history of benzodiazepine and opiate use.
rationales.F10: The absence of valvular vegetations on echocardiography makes Subacute bacterial endocarditis with embolic stroke less likely.
